does: Browns the surface of meat or fish fast in a very hot pan, building a crust full of flavour while the inside stays underdone.

intro.what: Searing browns the surface of meat or fish quickly in a very hot pan.
intro.why: It teaches you to control surface moisture and pan contact to build a flavourful crust.

how: Dry the surface well. Wet food steams before it browns.
Salt it just before it goes in.
Heat a heavy pan until a thin film of oil shimmers and gives off its first wisp of smoke.
Lay the food in away from you and press it flat. Then leave it alone.
Turn it when it lifts off the pan by itself and the underside is deep brown.
Take it out to rest. The crust left on the pan is the fond for a sauce.

cues.text: A loud, steady sizzle that does not fade. A weak hiss means the pan was not hot enough.
A deep brown crust, and a brown line climbing the side of the piece.
The piece lets go of the pan when it is ready to turn. If it sticks, it is not ready.

mistakes.mistake: Moving the food before it has browned, which tears the crust and leaves it on the pan.
mistakes.fix: Leave it until it releases by itself.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, so that the pieces stew in their own juice and turn grey.
mistakes.fix: Sear in batches with space between the pieces, and let the pan heat up again.

mistakes.mistake: Putting food in the pan while its surface is wet.
mistakes.fix: Pat it dry with paper on every side first.

quiz.question: What is the main aim of searing?
choices: To stew the food in its juices.
To build a browned, flavourful surface crust.
To keep the surface pale and wet.
quiz.because: Fast surface browning builds a crust full of flavour.

quiz.question: What does this method do before the food meets the pan?
quiz.because: Wet food steams before it browns. Dry the surface well before it meets the pan.

quiz.question: Which cue does this method use before turning a piece?
choices: It releases from the pan and has a deep brown underside.
It is still stuck and pale underneath.
Its surface is wet and the pan has fallen silent.
quiz.because: In this method, a deep brown underside and release from the pan are cues to turn rather than pull at a stuck surface.

quiz.question: Crowded pieces are stewing in their own juices. What would you change?
choices: Pack them closer to increase contact.
Sear in batches with room between pieces and reheat between them.
Cover the pan to trap more liquid.
quiz.because: Crowding makes pieces stew in their juices. Use batches with space between pieces and let the pan reheat.

comes_after.why: Sautéing teaches a hot pan and room between the pieces. Searing adds the hardest part: leaving the food alone.
